Italic-Solid-Serif.note: Two weights exist: 'Chapelries. Other Churches' is the heavier cut, the rest the lighter. They are told apart only by the terminals on lowercase s (sharp serif vs blob), which is below what a size-normalised glyph carries. Merged; if the distinction is ever needed, take it as a post-processing step on the spot's cap-height in map pixels, which normalisation discards.

Blackletter.note: Prehistoric/Saxon and Norman antiquities are drawn in blackletter, but the cut varies so much between instances that a human cannot reliably separate the two — tried and abandoned on the anchor review. Kept as ONE face: a distinction nobody can make by eye is not one to ask a matcher for, and splitting it would only manufacture disagreement between annotators.

_comment: Face inventory keyed by signature, not by OS Characteristic-Sheet category: one typeface commonly serves several CS categories at different sizes, so `os` lists them pipe-delimited. Only faces with at least one designation are kept — a permutation nobody has ever drawn is not a face. Blackletter is a letterform family rather than a slant, so it does not decompose into the fill/decor axes and its two faces are named for their OS categories.
